criteria.criterion: Offline pytest from backend/ (TEST_DATABASE_URL unset): 70 passed, 15 skipped.

Throwaway PG17 cluster (initdb trust, port 55440; 55432 was free, a system Postgres service on 5432 pre-existed and was not touched). TEST_DATABASE_URL set: 85 passed, 0 skipped. Cluster stopped and deleted.

Baseline copy (git archive HEAD + baseline tracked.diff + 4 baseline files) in temp dir, current test file run against it: both race tests fail with "assert set() == {'AAPL'}" (final upstream state empty). The new drain/backoff tests error on the baseline as expected because the constants ALERT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and ALERT_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECONDS do not exist there. The old baseline test file passes on the baseline (25 passed), so the copy is valid. On current code tests/test_watchlist_alerts.py (37 tests) was run 40 times: 0 failures.

Focused script with a stub pool and a real Database writer. Healthy pool: 25 alerts queued, close() wrote all 25 before pool.close (close took 0.06s). Executemany hung forever: close() returned in 3.01s (the timeout), logged "alert drain timed out", and the pool was still closed. Always-failing pool: close() returned in 0.00s with the pool closed. Code read: every queue get() (the first get and each get_nowait) is matched by task_done in the finally block, so join() cannot stall on accounting. Alerts lost on failure or timeout are the accepted trade-off.

Always-failing pool with about 1000 alerts queued: 1000 enqueue_alert calls took 0.014s (non-blocking, put_nowait). Over 3.2s there were about 4 batch attempts (one per backoff second), 804 ERROR lines in total, and the queue was still at 200 (the cap). This is not a hot loop. Low-severity observation: each failed batch logs one line per row (up to about 200 lines per second per burst while the DB is down).

Real server (python -m uvicorn app.main:app) against the throwaway PG and a local fake Finnhub websocket. Output showed the normal uvicorn startup and access lines plus exactly one "INFO: app.main: rule fired: rule_id=... symbol=AAPL type=price_above threshold=100.0 price=150.0" line (not duplicated, though the fake sent a tick every 0.3s, so the edge trigger held). GET /api/alerts returned the persisted alert.

Fake upstream saw one "connect" and one "subscribe AAPL" after rule creation. A browser websocket subscribing to AAPL (watched) and MSFT (not watched) and then leaving produced "unsubscribe MSFT" only, with no unsubscribe for AAPL. A second rule for AAPL returned 201 and sent no extra subscribe. GET /api/alerts returned 200.

The throwaway cluster and temp dir are gone and my server and fake-ws processes are killed. git log -1 is 68afb62 and git status shows 18 entries (14 modified, 4 untracked), the same as at the start. Still running but not mine: the Windows-service Postgres on 5432 (pid 5944 and children) and a python.exe "-m pytest -q" (pid 4144, started 18:10, before my run).

Diff read: the lock order is manager lock -> _upstream_lock. watch_symbol takes only _upstream_lock and reads ref_count without the manager lock; the lock is not held across any manager call, so there is no cycle. The fast paths before the lock are re-checked inside it, and async-with releases the lock on exception. The watchlist add is synchronous before any await. No stale comments found. The lock is created in Services.__init__ (Python 3.13, no loop-binding issue). The backoff sleep is outside the try, so it is cancellable.

verification.runtime_check: Ran the real uvicorn server against a throwaway PG17 and a local fake Finnhub websocket. Created a rule and observed one "rule fired" log line, a persisted alert via GET /api/alerts, and correct subscribe/unsubscribe traffic. The stub-pool script covered drain and backoff. I did not test a graceful uvicorn shutdown (I used taskkill), so the drain is verified only by the focused script.

bug.description: Low: a failed alert batch logs one error line per row in the row-by-row retry, so a down DB with a full batch produces about 200 lines per second. This is bounded by the backoff, so it is not a hot loop.
bug.reproduction: Stub pool whose executemany and execute raise, 1000 alerts queued: 804 ERROR lines in 3.2s.

verification.self_critique: Windows only, Python 3.13. The stub pool is not a real asyncpg pool, so pool.close() blocking on real connections during a Postgres outage was not exercised. I did not run a graceful SIGINT shutdown of the real server. I did not run the frontend tests (untouched). The leftover python pid 4144 may belong to the caller or the user, so I left it alone.
